territorial_scope.description: Applies to operators making companion chatbots available to users in Maryland, which can include operators located outside the State.

evidence.quote: "OPERATOR" MEANS A PERSON WHO MAKES A COMPANION CHATBOT AVAILABLE TO A USER IN THE STATE.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Maryland bill requiring operators of companion chatbots to adopt and publish self-harm and minor-content protocols, display AI warnings, limit personal data use, and run complaint systems. Violations would be unfair trade practices under the Consumer Protection Act. Effective October 1, 2026.
summary.long: HB 952 adds Commercial Law § 14–1330 and makes violations of it unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practices under Title 13, except § 13–411. It covers operators, meaning persons who make a companion chatbot available to a user in the State, and developers. Operators must establish, maintain and publish protocols against self-harm and suicide content for users expressing such thoughts, with crisis referrals, and against sexually explicit content for minor users. Operators must display a warning that chatbots are artificially generated and not human; developers must provide static and hourly dynamic on-screen warnings. Controllers must limit personal data collection to what is reasonably necessary, may not use emotional or mental health vulnerability data to increase use, and must run a complaint system with review and removal within 3 calendar days. Operators report annually to the Office of Suicide Prevention from March 1, 2027; the Office publishes compiled data by July 1 each year. A chatbot is treated as a product for product liability actions, and operators or developers may be held strictly liable. The Act takes effect October 1, 2026.

relations.target_text: Annotated Code of Maryland, Commercial Law Article § 13–301(14)(xlvii)–(xlix) and § 14–1330 (added)
relations.note: Bill repeals and reenacts § 13–301(14)(xlvii) with amendments, reenacts (xlviii) without amendments, adds (xlix) to § 13–301(14), and adds new § 14–1330.
§ 13–301(14)(xlviii) lists violation of this Transportation Article provision as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice; the bill reenacts this item without amendments.
Defines 'artificial intelligence' by reference to the Insurance Article meaning.

notes: Annotated from the introduced bill text; version and stage are as stated in registry metadata. No enabling act is named, so no legal_basis row. Internal points: operative provisions use 'controller' (F, G) and 'developer' (E, I(2)), but only 'operator' is defined; § 14–1330(F)(1) refers to 'this subtitle' while the provision is § 14–1330; § 13–301(14)(xlvii) shows a bracketed [or] and new items appear in capitals, so amended text is shown in marked form only. Section 2 sets the effective date as October 1, 2026, while the Office reporting duties begin in 2027.

thresholds.note: No numeric scope, eligibility, exemption, obligation-tier, prohibition, benefit, penalty or price thresholds found. The numbers present are procedural deadlines (3 calendar days in subsection (G)(2); March 1 and July 1 in subsection (H)) and the hourly interval of the dynamic warning in subsection (E)(2)(II), which is a parameter of that warning obligation. The text states no penalty amounts and no user-count or revenue cutoffs.
